(D)uplicate (D)oses Repeat Plot

Source: R/dd_repeat_plot.R
dd_repeat_plot.Rd

Generates two histograms comparing the age of vaccination of records identified as REPEATED. Shows the age at vaccination of the FIRST_ENTRYs in one histogram, while showing the age at vaccination of the REPEATED records in the other. Comparing both helps tell apart the possible causes of repeats: for example, if the repeats of DTP1 are concentrated at the age when DTP2 is due, then the "DTP1" dose may have been registered with the wrong dose number.

Usage

dd_repeat_plot(
  data,
  vaccine,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  within_ADM1 = NULL,
  binwidth = 7,
  max_age = NULL,
  data.schedule = NULL,
  schedule_vaccines = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The output from the immunabc::dd_duplicates function.

vaccine

Character. The single dose to show, e.g. "DTP1".

geo_level

Character. The geographic level of occurrence to split the panels by. Must be "ADM0" (default, no split), "ADM1" or "ADM2".

within_ADM1

Character (optional). A character vector of one or several "ADM1" areas of occurrence to filter. Default is NULL, which means no filtering by "ADM1".

binwidth

Numeric. Width of each bar of the histogram, in days. Default is 7 (one week).

max_age

Numeric (optional). Maximum age at vaccination, in days, to show on the x-axis. Records after that are not shown but their number is given in the caption. Default is NULL, which shows all ages.

data.schedule

Data frame (optional). A data frame defining the vaccination schedule, used to show the vaccination window of the doses in schedule_vaccines. See immunABC.schedule for expected structure. Default is NULL, which shows no schedule.

schedule_vaccines

Character (optional). Up to 3 doses whose vaccination window is highlighted, e.g. c("DTP1", "DTP2"). Only used with data.schedule. If NULL (default), the vaccination window of vaccine is highlighted.

Value

A ggplot object representing the histogram.

Details

When the user provides data.schedule, a shaded area highlights the vaccination window of each dose in schedule_vaccines (using age_schedule_low and age_schedule_high). Results can also be split into columns of panels per geographic area of occurrence with geo_level.

Records with no date_birth have no age at vaccination, and records with date_vax before date_birth have a negative one, so both are filtered out, with a message.
